road.title: Where you are from
road.description: A small, square figure wrapped in a scarf of regulation length, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Eudora is a Border Official and administers a border that moved away one night and stamps papers so that it will know where to come back to.

character.name: Eudora Cobbett
character.description: A small, square figure wrapped in a scarf of regulation length, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Eudora is a Border Official and administers a border that moved away one night and stamps papers so that it will know where to come back to.

npc.narrative: The pioggia hammers the fienile like a creditor, and each fulmine lights a tavolo, a lanterna and a timbro set out in the middle of the campo. Eudora Cobbett holds an ombrello over the carte and none over herself. She counts you with the hope of a dispari number, and the inchiostro runs regardless.
npc.native: Buonasera! Sono Eudora Cobbett, e sono di qui, anche se il confine non è più qui. Vengo da una casa vicina, abito vicino alla strada e parlo solo questa lingua. Conto tutti quelli che passano con questa pioggia. Raccontami di te: da dove arrivi, dove stai di solito, come parli con me e che cosa pensi del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: Good evening! I am Eudora Cobbett, and I am from here, even if the border is no longer here. I come from a house nearby, I live near the road and I speak only this language. I count everyone who passes in this rain. Tell me about yourself: where do you come from, where do you usually stay, how do you speak with me and what do you think of my work?

correction.translation: Good evening Eudora! I am from England.

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice start: you greeted Eudora and told her where you are from in Italian. Next, try telling her where you live and how you speak with her.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you said where you are from with "Sono di"; with a country the natural form is "Sono dell'Inghilterra".
You haven't told Eudora where you live yet; she will ask again, so have a go next time.
You haven't said that you speak a little of her language yet; Eudora will ask again later.

correction.translation: Good evening Eudora! I am from England.

openObjectives.prompt: Tell Eudora where you live, using Italian.
Eudora has noticed your accent and is being polite about it, with visible effort. Tell Eudora that you speak a little of their language, using Italian.

npc.narrative: La pioggia drums on the tetto of the garitta, and un fulmine shows Eudora's stamp hovering sopra a foglio. She marks you on a lavagna, then counts again, piano, because the numero is not yet right.
npc.native: Inghilterra! Che nome lontano. Con te sono dodici persone stasera, e dodici è un numero pari: che delusione. Io abito vicino alla strada e vivo qui da sempre. E tu, dove abiti adesso, e come parli con me in questa lingua?
npc.translation: England! What a faraway name. With you that makes twelve people tonight, and twelve is an even number: what a disappointment. I live near the road and I have lived here forever. And you, where do you live now, and how do you speak with me in this language?

player: Abito a Londra. Parlo... un po' italiano.

correction.text: Abito a Londra. Parlo un po' di italiano.
correction.translation: I live in London. I speak a little Italian.

verdict.overallFeedback: You told Eudora where you live and that you speak a little Italian, and both came across clearly. Only a tiny \"di\" was missing.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: "Abito a Londra" tells Eudora clearly where you live.
Good: "Parlo" is right. Just add "di" after "un po'": "un po' di italiano".

correction.text: Abito a Londra. Parlo un po' di italiano.
correction.translation: I live in London. I speak a little Italian.

npc.narrative: The pioggia drums on the roof of the booth, and Eudora lowers her grande timbro onto your carta with great cura. Outside, a cane trots in the erba beside the strada, not on it, and the notte is molto scura.
npc.native: Londra! Abiti a Londra e parli un po' di italiano: il timbro è pronto. Ho contato di nuovo: siamo tredici, un numero dispari, e sono molto contenta. Che cosa pensi del mio lavoro, e come passi la serata con questa pioggia?
npc.translation: London! You live in London and you speak a little Italian: the stamp is ready. I counted again: we are thirteen, an odd number, and I am very happy. What do you think of my work, and how are you spending the evening in this rain?

player: Non capisco. E tu? Di dove sei?

npc.narrative: It is notte, and the cielo is grigio. Eudora puts down her timbro and looks at you as if the confine had asked its own age. Behind her the strada goes on into the buio, and a cane waits in the erba beside it, not on it.
npc.native: Io sono di qui, naturalmente! Il confine non è più qui, ma io sono sempre qui, e metto il timbro sui documenti. Parlo piano, così capisci meglio. Tu puoi chiedermi del mio lavoro: che cosa vuoi sapere, e che cosa fai tu a Londra ogni giorno?
npc.translation: I am from here, naturally! The border is no longer here, but I am always here, and I put the stamp on the papers. I speak slowly, so you understand better. You can ask me about my work: what do you want to know, and what do you do in London every day?

player: Lavoro a Londra... sono teacher. Grazie, arrivederci!

npc.narrative: You have one piede on the strada when Eudora lifts your carta by the corner, the timbro still wet. Above the posto di blocco the cielo is grey and has made no piani. In the erba beside the road, a cane sits and watches the ultima stretch as if it were owed money.
npc.native: Insegnante! È un bel lavoro, quasi come il mio. Aspetta un momento, il timbro non è ancora asciutto. Prima delle nove riorganizzazioni tutto era meglio, ma questa è un'altra storia. Che cosa insegni a Londra, e che cosa vuoi sapere del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: Teacher! It is a fine job, almost like mine. Wait a moment, the stamp is not dry yet. Before the nine reorganisations everything was better, but that is another story. What do you teach in London, and what do you want to know about my work?

npc.narrative: It is dawn, and the sky is chiaro, which Eudora takes as a personal favour. She blows on the timbro, then counts the people on the strada again, piano, with her lips moving. Beside the road, in the erba, the dog waits for her to finish.
npc.native: Insegni inglese, che bel lavoro! Io parlo solo questa lingua e non ne conosco altre. Qui nessuno ne parla un'altra, perché non serve. Come sono i tuoi studenti, e che cosa vuoi sapere del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: You teach English, what a fine job! I speak only this language and I don't know any others. Here nobody speaks another one, because it isn't needed. What are your students like, and what do you want to know about my work?
